elowen.title: Bedside Manner
elowen.text: Elowen insists on a "check-up" and spends most of it nervously talking about herbs, rosemary in her braid, fingers pressed to your pulse a few seconds longer than the instructions require. The room smells of chamomile and lamp oil. At the end she admits she's never been this far from home, and that you make it feel less far.

choices.label: Tell her the distance feels shorter to you too
choices.res: She keeps her fingers on your wrist and doesn't count anything. The tea goes cold between them, and neither says what the silence is for.

choices.label: Offer to be her patient any time
choices.res: "Any time," you say. {N} hides behind her sleeve, ears pink, and writes "weekly" in her notes before you can see it.

image.comp: pressing a stethoscope-like charm to his chest, nervously babbling about herbs
image.setting: small infirmary with herbs drying from the rafters

elowen.title: Tea Service
elowen.text: Elowen brings herbal tea to your room at exactly the moment you're changing, the tray balanced carefully in both hands, a little steam rising off the pot. She sees. The tray hits the floor with a crash of porcelain, and the smell of mint and lemon balm rises from the rug. You stand frozen with one arm in a sleeve, and neither of them breathes.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.res: She laughs too, eventually, from behind both hands, shoulders shaking. They pick up the shards together, not quite looking up.

choices.label: Apologize profusely
choices.res: They both apologize to each other for ten minutes, bowing in turn like two clockwork birds, and the broken teapot is never mentioned again.

choices.label: "You're a healer. You've seen it all, right?"
choices.res: "Not... all," she says faintly, fanning her flushed face with a hand.

else.res: She turns red to the tips of her pointed ears and mutters something about anatomy textbooks, then kneels very fast to gather the shattered cups.

image.comp: dropping a tea tray in a doorway, hands over her face, peeking through her fingers
image.setting: small bedroom, spilled tea on the floor

elowen.title: Flower Crowns
elowen.text: They go flower-picking outside the walls "for medicine," a basket on Elowen's arm and the smell of crushed clover under their boots. Somewhere in the second hour the herb list is forgotten. Elowen weaves you a flower crown with quick, careful fingers. You make a terrible one back, lopsided and shedding petals. She wears it all day.

choices.label: Wear her crown home
choices.res: You wear hers all the way back through the gate, pollen on your collar, and don't mind the guards' stares. She walks half a step closer than usual.

choices.label: Tell her the lopsided one suits her
choices.res: "It suits you," you say of your own wreck. {N} adjusts it on her braid with immense seriousness and says it is the finest crown in Hollowmere.

image.comp: placing a flower crown on his head in a meadow, holding the lopsided one he made her
image.setting: wildflower meadow outside town walls, sunny afternoon

elowen.title: Burnout
elowen.text: Elowen has been healing the dock workers for free, every night, for weeks, coming home with salt on her hem and shadows under her green eyes. Today she collapses in the kitchen mid-sentence about willow bark. Her rosemary sprig has come loose from her braid, and her hands are cold.

choices.label: Scold her
choices.res: She cries. Not because you're wrong. The rosemary stays on the floor where it fell, and she doesn't speak to you until morning.

choices.label: Take care of her for a day
choices.res: You make soup (badly), read to her (badly, doing the voices), and don't leave her side. She sleeps for fourteen hours, one hand curled in your sleeve.

choices.label: Fund a free clinic night (150g)
choices.res: One night a week, with help from the apothecary's apprentices. She hugs you so hard your ribs creak, and presses her damp face against your hoodie.

cantAfford.res: You can't afford it. She thanks you for trying.

image.comp: collapsed against kitchen cabinets, exhausted, healer's satchel spilled, the man kneeling beside her

elowen.title: Starlight
elowen.text: Elowen takes you to a hill outside town on a cloudless night, the grass cool and damp, and names the constellations of her homeland, one by one, in the soft old language of the cedar glade. Her finger traces lines across the dark. Her voice grows steadier with every name, and further away.

choices.label: Listen to every single one
choices.res: There are a lot of them. You don't mind. By the last one her head is on your shoulder, and she's stopped pointing.

choices.label: Make up a constellation for her
choices.res: "The Clumsy Healer." She shoves you. She uses the name forever, and writes it into the margins of her star chart in tiny, careful script.

image.comp: pointing up at the night sky from a hilltop, naming constellations, the man beside her
image.setting: grassy hilltop at night, sweeping starry sky

elowen.title: Long-Lived
elowen.text: Elowen kisses you first, very quickly, in the herb garden after dusk with moths circling the lamp, then hides her face in your shirt. "Elves live a long time," she mumbles into the grey cotton. "I'd like to spend some of it with you." Her braid smells of rosemary and rain. She doesn't let go of your hand all the way to her room.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods against your chest, embarrassed and relieved. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She's still holding your sleeve.
